repo.description: Git URL of the upstream harness.

binary.description: Name of the executable the harness installs, e.g. opencode.

installer.description: The harness's official installer. When a user installs a mod for a harness they do not have, the CLI shows this command and runs it if they say yes.

command.description: Shell command from the harness's own install docs, e.g. curl -fsSL https://opencode.ai/install | bash.

paths.description: Folders the installer puts the binary in (~ is the home folder), so it is found before a new shell picks up the PATH line the installer added.

requirements.description: What a build needs on the machine, checked before anything is fetched or built. Each is a command that must be on PATH, or a check, a shell command that must succeed (for a library, say), on every OS or only on os.

os.description: Only on this OS, as Node names it.

hint.description: What to install, shown when it is missing.

install.description: Shell command run in the checkout root before building.

build.description: Shell command run in the checkout root that produces the artifact.

artifact.description: Path of the built executable relative to the checkout root. {os} and {arch} are substituted with Node's process.platform and process.arch.

keep.description: The folder, relative to the harness checkout, that holds the binary and everything it needs beside it, such as helper executables and resources. It is copied whole for each build, and artifact must be inside it. When unset, only the binary is kept.

dev.description: Shell command that runs a clone of the harness from source, for `openmods dev`. {root} is the clone's path and {version} a version like 1.18.32+my-mod-dev; the user's arguments are appended. It runs in the user's project folder with the release's pinned toolchain on PATH, and should end in exec.

env.description: Environment variables the modded build runs with, and a clone under `openmods dev`. For settings a modded build needs, such as turning off the harness's own self-update, since OpenMods offers the updates.

args.description: Arguments the modded build, and a clone under `openmods dev`, always start with, before the user's. For a setting a modded build needs that has no environment variable, such as turning off Codex's update check, since OpenMods offers the updates.

releaseTagPattern.description: Glob for release tags, used by the compatibility checker.

typecheck.description: Shell command run in the checkout root that type-checks the harness without producing a binary, e.g. cargo check or tsc. The release watch uses it to verify mods against a new release; the full build runs once per harness release and on a mod's pull request.

recipe.description: What our install, typecheck and build commands depend on in the harness's repo. When a new release changes any of it, the release watch holds the harness's mods until a person runs the harness build workflow. Each entry watches a whole file, or only its lines matching `lines` (a regex).
